decision: Standing user choice for this run: every rule that clears the precision gate enters the queue, nothing is deferred. All five rules are PASS with queue_eligible true in 01.5-precision-report.json -- RMIC_TOOL_REMOVED 2/2 census at 1.0, WRAPPER_CONSTRUCTOR_DEPRECATED_FOR_REMOVAL 30 judged of a 147-hit population at 0.9667, APPLET_API_DEPRECATED_FOR_REMOVAL 8/8 census at 1.0 (pattern revision 2), MULTICAST_SOCKET_GROUP_API_DEPRECATED 2/2 census at 1.0, and THREADGROUP_DESTROY_DEPRECATED_FOR_REMOVAL 1/1 census at 1.0 (pattern revision 2). RMIC_TOOL_REMOVED (HIGH) is the only mandatory breaking change and the only thing standing between this workspace and a green build on JDK 17; the two MEDIUM and two LOW rules are deprecation work queued under the same standing choice rather than deferred. The on-disk order is by severity. The binding execution order is computed by effective_rule_order, which ranks body-local ahead of signature, so APPLET_API_DEPRECATED_FOR_REMOVAL (the only signature-class rule) runs last. BUILD_JAVAC_SOURCE_TARGET_17 is deliberately absent: it cleared the gate at 1.0 but build_audit.py had already applied source/target 17 at BUILD_GATE_READY, so queueing it would mean queueing a rule with zero remaining flags. It is recorded in the manifest's withdrawn_rules with that reasoning.
